what_it_does: Recommendation systems — the kind that decide what ad or product to show you — train on multiple GPUs that each hold a piece of a giant lookup table called an embedding table (a massive dictionary that maps items like products to numerical descriptions). Training requires each GPU to look up its local entries and then share results with the others in a collective communication step; the problem is that which entries each GPU needs depends entirely on the current batch of user data, making the communication pattern unpredictable and impossible to accelerate with existing network hardware. TRACI moves the aggregation work into the network switches themselves (the routers that connect the GPUs), so that when two GPUs happen to ask for the same embedding, the switch combines or deduplicates their requests on the fly rather than sending redundant data all the way to each host. New hardware in the switch reads small tags on each message that identify which data can be reused, enabling this dynamic merging. This is based on the abstract and specific throughput gains would need to be confirmed from the full paper.
